answer: A practical defence is Proof of unique council tax account. It rests on a tax account held at one address for a decade, which gives every honest agent a reef that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since a tax account held at one address for a decade takes calendar time as well as money — and the plume is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The willow is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
